title: PR gate follow-ups from RF-100: robust self-check, base-branch gate scripts, closed-PR label runs
acceptance: pr-gates.sh self-check reads the workflows' job names, concurrency groups and status context structurally (parsed YAML), so a reformat that keeps the meaning (quoting, indentation, a folded line) does not fail CI and a real rename still does.

The owner-gate jobs run the base branch's copy of .github/scripts/pr-gates.sh (as they already do for owner-gate.mjs and rf-trace.mjs), or the PR documents why the PR-controlled copy is acceptable; the trust model is stated in AGENTS.md.

A label change on a closed or merged PR starts no Owner gate job, or the skipped run is documented as harmless; reopening still re-evaluates the gate through owner-gate.yml (RF-176 moved the gate there).
Once RF-176 is on main, pr-gates.sh gate-status drops its transitional branch for a pre-RF-176 checker that writes no OWNER_GATE_RESULT verdict, so every missing verdict is an error.
nextAction: Owner triages: decide whether the gate-script trust change is worth it for a guardrail that AGENTS.md already calls not a security boundary.

evidence.summary: Review findings on #700 deferred out of RF-100: self-check greps exact YAML lines (brittle to reformatting); both workflows run the PR's own pr-gates.sh and workflow files (pre-existing trust model: a PR can edit its own gate); label events on closed PRs still start an Owner gate run whose jobs skip.
